items.body_excerpt:
Tiago Splitter gave Noa Essengue an ultimatum at the start of this season — if he wants to play, he has to guard. Hard. Every play.

So far, the kid has done his best to deliver. 

On Noa’s growing pains and the subtle development taking place this season:

items.title: Jonathan Kuminga spent most of his career among the league's more ball-dominant players: 75th–88th percentile in On Ball %. With the Wolves he's at 8.0%, 9th percentile. Early sample, but that's a real shift in how he plays.
items.body_excerpt:
Jonathan Kuminga spent most of his career among the league's more ball-dominant players: 75th–88th percentile in On Ball %. With the Wolves he's at 8.0%, 9th percentile. Early sample, but that's a real shift in how he plays.

On Ball %: Share of offensive time player is holding or dribbling the ball

images.alt:
Column chart titled "Jonathan Kuminga On Ball %," with the subtitle "Share of offensive time player is holding or dribbling the ball." Six bars show each season's On Ball % with its league percentile, colored by team with the team logo inside.

2022, Golden State Warriors: 12.6%, 75th percentile
2023, Golden State Warriors: 13.1%, 81st percentile
2024, Golden State Warriors: 16.0%, 85th percentile
2025, Golden State Warriors: 20.4%, 88th percentile
2026, split diagonally between the Golden State Warriors and Atlanta Hawks: 18.8%, 79th percentile
2027, Minnesota Timberwolves: 8.0%, 9th percentile

His On Ball % rose each season through 2025, dipped slightly in 2026, then fell sharply to 8.0% in 2027. A footnote says the 2027 season is in progress. Data: DataballR. Viz: @Hoopinformatics.com on Bluesky.

items.title: Victor Wembanyama is coming up with an answer for everything.
items.body_excerpt:
Victor Wembanyama is coming up with an answer for everything.

www.expressnews.com/sports/spurs...

images.alt:
One by one, Victor Wembanyama collects new bits of jargon, new idioms, and new little slices of American English slang. After more than three years in his adopted country, some discoveries still delight him.
For instance, he now knows that when a teammate overshares personal details, hypothetically about bodily functions, an appropriate reply might be to say, "T.M.I.," for "too much information."
"I just learned that one five days ago," Wembanyama said
Wednesday night.
At this rate, it won't be long until he has an answer for everything. It won't be long until the Spurs' most rapacious seeker of knowledge develops a countermove for every conversational faux pas, for every defensive adjustment, and even for every shooting slump.
In fact, that last one he already might have mastered. When it became clear during the Spurs' 112-111 victory over the Mavericks at Frost Bank Center that neither Wembanyama nor his sidekicks could make a perimeter shot to save their lives, he realized there was an obvious response.
T.M.I.
Take more inside.
"The team who's willing to get to the rim more usually is successful," said the 7-foot-4 Frenchman who'd just scored 52 points to prove it.
